title: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana Taxation: Decoding SSY's EEE Status
description: The Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY) offers a triple tax benefit, commonly known as the Exempt-Exempt-Exempt (EEE) status. Contributions made to an SSY account .

faq.q: Can I open an SSY account for my adopted daughter?
faq.a: Yes, an SSY account can be opened for an adopted girl child, provided she meets the age criteria. The adoption certificate would serve as proof of relationship.

faq.q: What happens if I miss a minimum deposit in a financial year?
faq.a: If the minimum deposit of ₹250 is not made in a financial year, the account becomes irregular. It can be regularised by paying a penalty of ₹50 for each year of default, along with the minimum deposit amount for those years.

faq.q: Can an NRI girl child have an SSY account?
faq.a: No, the Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana is exclusively for resident Indian girl children. If a girl child who is an account holder becomes a Non-Resident Indian (NRI), the account will be closed from the date of her becoming an NRI, and no interest will be payable from that date.

faq.q: Is there a limit on the number of SSY accounts per family?
faq.a: A guardian can open a maximum of two SSY accounts for two different girl children. Exceptions are made for twins or triplets born in the first or second instance of birth.

faq.q: What is the current interest rate for SSY?
faq.a: The interest rate for Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana is declared quarterly by the Ministry of Finance. It is advisable to check the official notifications on the Ministry of Finance website for the latest applicable rate.

faq.q: Can I withdraw money before the girl child turns 18?
faq.a: No, partial withdrawals are only permitted once the girl child attains the age of 18 years or has passed the 10th standard, whichever is earlier.
